newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Greek troops will be stationed in Tirana and Vlore, following agreement between Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos and his Italian counterpart. The majority of the 700 troops will be placed in the Albanian capital.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis appears determined to press ahead with his controversial changes to labour relations, despite the objections of unionists, government members and the reservations of the labour ministry. Sources say his speech today at the Economist roundtable with the Greek government will expand on his positions and that the prime minister is determined to proceed with "courage and decisiveness".

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos was harsh in his reservations about the state of democracy in certain candidates for NATO membership, saying NATO member Turkey was no model of democracy when it came to respect for human rights and freedom of expression.
--Parliament yesterday approved a bill that will provide MPs with retroactive payments of up to 25 million drachmas per deputy. The measure must be approved by the finance ministry.
--The finance ministry is battling tax department employees who, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou is reported to have said, are interfering in the running of the ministry.
--New Democracy's new president Costa Karamanlis set out his positions in his maiden speech on the Greek economy at last night's Economist conference.

--The total bill for retroactive payment for MPs will come to 7.5 billion drachmas. The legislation was supported by ruling PASOK, opposition New Democracy and Coalition of the Left and Progress deputies, but opposed by Communist Party and Democratic Social Movement MPs.
--Nine mayors in the Attica region yesterday decided on the establishment of a joint committee to look into introducing trams that will connect the centre of Athens with the coastal road.
--Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos is planning changes to the guidelines for the temporary transfer of civil servants to other services.
--Confidential documents appear to show that Greek-Turkish dialogue on the differences in the Aegean has already begun in Brussels under the auspices of NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.

--Thirty-nine doctors working in the state health system face dismissal for prescribing medicines totalling 7.5-20.2 million drachmas in one month. The limit for prescriptions is three million drachmas.

--Democratic Social Movement leader Dimitris Tsovolas yesterday crossed swords in court with maverick 'Avriani' publisher George Kouris. Kouris and two of his reporters received 15 months' jail for defamation, after Tsovolas sued over pre-election allegations regarding his Voula home. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
